claim.claim-text: 2. A method of claim 1, wherein the page end criteria occurs based, at least in part, on reaching a packet header whose connection field requests closing a connection associated with the web page, the subsequent HTTP transaction is not part of the web page, or both.

the page end criteria occurs based, at least in part, on an elapsed time between receipt of subsequent HTTP transaction for the web page exceeding a predetermined threshold and a page cache entry for the web page specifies a transaction for the web page has closed; and the page cache maintains, at least in part, a status for open web pages.
4. A method of claim 1, wherein the detecting is based on examination of a first packet in the HTTP page-start transaction.
5. A method of claim 4, wherein the examination further comprises:
determining if a status line of the first packet includes a value of 200; and determining if a header of the first packet includes a content-type entry indicative of HTML content.
6. A method of claim 4, wherein the examination further comprises:

generating a unique ID for the a browser requesting the web page; creating an entry for the browser in an early classification cache based, at least in part, on the ID; and designating a timestamp for the entry creation as the start of the web page, wherein the early classification cache maintains, at least in part, a status for open web pages.
7. A method of claim 6, wherein the determining further comprises:

determining whether a header in the subsequent HTTP start transaction includes a referrer field which matches an open entry in the early classification cache; and designating the subsequent HTTP transaction as part of the web page.
8. A method of claim 1, wherein the assigning further comprises examining a header of a first packet to determine a protocol for the HTTP page-start transaction.

9. A method of claim 1, wherein the page classification is assigned based on a classification entry associated with a server domains and/or domain names in a first packet and stored in a classification cache.
10. A method of claim 1, wherein the determining further comprises:

determining whether a header in the subsequent HTTP transaction includes a referrer field which identifies the HTTP page-start transaction; and designating the subsequent HTTP transaction as part of the web page.
11. A method of claim 10, further comprising:

recursively parsing referrer fields in subsequent HTTP transactions; and designating a subsequent HTTP transaction as part of the web page if its referrer field identifies a previous parsed HTTP transaction or the HTTP page-start transaction.
